claims.statement: The renderer builds the entire LLM request but can only place the literal sentinel API_KEY_SENTINEL ('{{apiKey}}') where the key goes; the Rust shell substitutes the real key by replacing the sentinel across every header value (build_call_headers) just before sending, and a keyless (noKey) target instead drops every sentinel-bearing header and sends the rest.

There are eleven providers (anthropic, openai, google, openrouter, groq, mistral, deepseek, xai, openai-compatible, systemone, ollama); openai-compatible, systemone (default https://api.typesafe.ai), and ollama (localhost:11434) have editable base URLs; supportsModelListing is false for openai-compatible and systemone (no safe endpoint/shape to assume for an arbitrary self-hosted server or a decision model).

supportsPdf is false for groq, mistral, deepseek, xai, openai-compatible, systemone, and ollama (no single inline-attachment request), so a target set to send the PDF against them silently falls back to extracted text at run time; buildRequest throws on a PDF for ollama and the store always sends text.

Each provider carries a tokenParam of 'max_tokens' or 'max_completion_tokens' to avoid the OpenAI-specific rename trap: OpenAI/Groq/xAI require max_completion_tokens on newer models while OpenRouter/Mistral/DeepSeek/self-hosted servers still use max_tokens; sending the wrong one fails the call.

buildRequest produces four genuinely different request shapes: Anthropic (POST /v1/messages, x-api-key, body with max_tokens/system/messages, adaptive thinking + output_config.effort), Google (model in URL path, x-goog-api-key, generateContent body), Ollama (native POST /api/chat with options.num_ctx — never /v1/chat/completions, which cannot set the context window), and OpenAI-shaped (POST /v1/chat/completions, Bearer auth, the provider's tokenParam); systemone never goes through buildRequest at all.

For Google, reasoning effort switches between thinkingLevel (named, Gemini 3.x via googleThinkingMechanism) and thinkingBudget (a token count derived from the chosen level via GOOGLE_BUDGET_BY_LEVEL, Gemini 2.5.x); the two are mutually exclusive and sending both is an error.
Reasoning effort for OpenAI-shaped providers is sent as reasoning_effort (flat) for all except OpenRouter, which takes { reasoning: { effort } } (nested).

DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS is deliberately generous (8192) because on reasoning-capable models the output budget is shared between hidden reasoning tokens and the visible answer; reasoning can exhaust the whole budget before any visible token is written, surfacing as a truncation flag with no usable text rather than an error.

Provider response reading is deliberately tolerant: extractText degrades to '' and extractError always yields something readable (including the Ollama 404 'pull the model first' hint and the Cloudflare {success, errors[]} envelope); wasTruncated distinguishes a 2xx response cut off by the token budget from the model having nothing to say, letting the store give a targeted 'budget exhausted on reasoning' message instead of 'the reply was empty'.

Model discovery resolves each provider's list-models endpoint into flat ModelInfo {id, label, reasoning}; reasoning is read from the response where the provider says so (Anthropic capabilities.effort, Google thinking flag, OpenRouter supported_efforts) and otherwise inferred from a model-ID pattern (OpenAI o[0-9]/gpt-5 excluding -chat, Groq gpt-oss, xAI grok-4.5, Mistral small/medium).

DeepSeek and openai-compatible are deliberately left with no reasoning-effort control (DeepSeek's contract unconfirmed, self-hosted servers have no single shape), so the app never offers a control that silently does nothing on some servers.

The list-models pagination cursor is resolved as a URL against the base and rejected if it leaves the origin (resolveSameOrigin); this prevents a malicious cursor like '@evil.com/v1/models' parsing as userinfo and redirecting an API-key-bearing request to an attacker host.

fetchModels is cached per config id for MODELS_TTL_MS (1 hour) to make reopening the settings dialog instant; an explicit force refresh bypasses it, it never attempts openai-compatible, and it walks at most MAX_MODEL_PAGES (10) pages as a backstop.

The system prompt teaches the model how an annotation schema is written (SCHEMA_FORMAT_DOC mirroring docs/annotation-schema.md §3) before showing one, so it reads an unfamiliar schema rather than pattern-matches; the format doc and the docs page must move together.

buildSystemPrompt is delivery-aware: when the paper arrives as extracted text it adds a rule warning the extraction is lossy (tables/figures/layout may be garbled, do not reconstruct illegible content), so the model does not confidently reconstruct a mangled table.

Every prompt rule pushes the model toward omitting a field rather than inventing one: ground values in the paper with no outside knowledge, omit fields the paper does not answer, quote a verbatim snippet of evidence for every value (or omit it), respect field types, and match enum options verbatim.

extractPdfText reconstructs reading-order lines by bucketing pdf.js items by baseline y and sorting each bucket by x (naive item-order join of a two-column paper is soup), normalizes to NFC after the join, and flags empty below EMPTY_CHAR_THRESHOLD (200 chars) as a scanned/image-only PDF that the run refuses to send.

parseAnswer is the trust boundary of the AI feature and never throws; it returns fields (accepted Suggestion[]), skipped (fields left empty with reasons), and rejected (refused suggestions kept and shown, because a silently dropped answer looks like the model said nothing).

extractObject tolerates a direct JSON parse, a ```json fence (with tag often missing/misspelled), and a balanced-brace scanner that knows about string literals/escapes (a regex cannot do this: a non-greedy match stops at the first '}' which usually sits inside a quoted evidence string).

Coercion bends only where there is exactly one honest reading: "2021" becomes number 2021, "true"/"True" becomes boolean, a case- or whitespace-off enum answer is snapped to its canonical option; everything else ("about 20", a value not in the enum, an empty string, a number for a string field) is rejected, never guessed.

Confidence outside 0..1 is dropped to null rather than clamped, because a model answering 95 may mean percent or a 1..100 scale; an empty string is not confidence 0 (Number('') is 0 inside the range).

resolvePath checks paths against the schema (not the current data) so the model may name an index that does not exist yet to record a further entry of a repeatable node; missing instances are created at apply time.

The maxUnboundedIndex option (MAX_UNBOUNDED_INDEX = 10000) is opt-in and only the LLM entry points opt in, because materializing every instance up to a named index makes a huge index an out-of-memory kill; applying the ceiling everywhere silently dropped real data in git/merge.ts.

Node names may contain /, [, ], or \ and are escaped with a backslash; a name with none of these characters must escape to itself for byte-compatibility, because canonical path strings are persisted (they key paper.equal marks and AI-mark keys).

isUnanswered matches validate.ts's empty notion for strings/numbers but booleans have their own rule: a boolean is offered unless already true (the AI can propose flipping to true, never to false, and never clears a ticked box), because the data model cannot represent an unanswered boolean.

useAiStore owns the AI flow as a phase state machine (setup → reading → starting → calling → parsing → review → applied/error; 'starting' starts an app-managed local System One model before the first call) and is kept separate from the main store; the only bridge is apply(), which hands checked rows to the main store's applyAiSuggestionsBatch as a single undo step that never overwrites a reviewer and leaves no trace when it writes nothing.

The finished run's target is recorded (runUsage) when the run starts and apply reads it rather than the current selection, so a reply about paper A cannot be written onto paper B while the dialog, paper list, seat picker, and target picker stay usable in flight; a superseded run returns silently rather than publishing or narrating over the replacement.

At review most suggestion rows are pre-ticked (rowChecked: judge accept, or System One confidence ≥ threshold; null confidence stays ticked) so the reviewer's job is to remove what is wrong, and the initial tick decision is mirrored into flagged so the needs-attention filter survives re-ticking; apply passes only the checked rows.

cancel aborts only and does not clear the controller slot (clearing it there made the run's own catch unable to tell an abort from a failure); the run clears the slot itself when it settles if it is still current. skipPaper aborts a single paper's own controller, recording it in skippedPapers (not errors) so it stays a resume candidate.

verifyConfig saves the target first (the key must be stored before use), sends the smallest request that reliably answers ('Reply with OK'), uses a 2048-token budget below the real run, and distinguishes empty reply from budget-exhausted-on-reasoning via wasTruncated.

applyAiSuggestions is the only place model output reaches the project data and guarantees: it never overwrites the reviewer (a field answered since or a path that no longer resolves is skipped), the whole fill is one undo step, and a run that writes nothing leaves no trace.

applyAiSuggestionsBatch refuses at apply time if the project is multi-reviewer with no seat, the seat is Consolidation, or it is a screening project (screening applies via its own applyAiScreeningBatch); a batch applied from the AI's own seat bypasses the no-seat/Consolidation refusals because it writes into the AI seat, and per-item replacements only write when the field still equals the checked value.

applyAiSuggestionsBatch usage comes from the recorded run usage (provider/model), not the current target selection, so switching the target between reply and Apply does not record the wrong provider/model.

aiMarks is session-only (lives beside the project, never serialized to disk) and marks fields the app filled that the reviewer has not looked at; useAiMark exposes the marked/confirm pair and confirmAiMark drops the mark.

AiUsageRecord is a persisted disclosure record appended to paper.aiUsage only when a fill actually changes something, recording provider, model, the Apply timestamp, the mode ('prompt'|'agent'|'classify'|'screening'), judge model and verdicts, rounds, few-shot, edited and rechecked/replaced counts, web searches, and the reviewer; AiUsageDisclosure shows them seat-filtered (a reviewer sees own plus unattributed, Consolidation sees all).

LlmSettingsDialog enforces the key-invariant in the UI: an existing key is only ever hasKey (never shown/pre-filled), leaving the key box blank on an edit keeps the stored key, and Verify saves the target first because the key must be stored before anything can use it.

Switching provider resets the base URL, clears the model and reasoning effort (they belong to the old catalog), and clears the fetched model list; a reasoning-effort selector appears only for a model with a ReasoningProfile and a useEffect keeps reasoningEffort in step with the selected model.

ModelPicker is deliberately not ComboBox: the model field is a free-text input the reviewer can always type into (a catalog may be incomplete or unfetched), with a searchable dropdown and a red invalid flag judged only against a list actually fetched (an empty list means unknown, never invalid).

Each call carries a requestId so the renderer's AbortSignal maps to a separate llm:abort command that the Rust Flight registry (net.rs) matches against the in-flight request; the CallResult also carries a parsed Retry-After (delta-seconds or IMF-fixdate HTTP date) as retry_after_ms.

The llm:call handler re-derives the configured origin and refuses to send the key unless the request URL scheme is http/https and matches the base scheme, and the origin matches exactly — preventing a compromised renderer posting the key to a host of its choosing, and avoiding a file: base authorizing any file: target.

The llm:call handler sends with a reqwest client with no document origin (no CORS preflight), refuses redirects both via the NO_REDIRECT policy and by treating any 3xx status as an error (following one would carry the substituted key past the origin check), and enforces a 10-minute LLM_TIMEOUT via the net.rs Flight abort/timeout registry.
join appends a path to a base URL without duplicating what the user already typed, accepting http://host:1234, …/v1, or the full …/v1/chat/completions as the endpoint for openai-compatible.

An API key never lives in the renderer: LlmConfig has no apiKey field; the Rust shell stores keys in the OS keychain via the keyring crate (service 'SaiLoR', entry 'llm:<id>'), and configs persist in config_dir/SaiLoR/llm-config.json (mode 0600, Mutex-serialized read-modify-write) keeping the Electron format with a '"keyring": true' marker per keyed entry — legacy Electron safeStorage blobs are kept but cannot be decrypted, so such keys must be entered once more; the renderer only ever sees hasKey/noKey and there is no read-back path.

A call for an app-managed local model (managed.catalogId) is started lazily by llm:call: the stored base URL is only a placeholder the origin checks pinned the request to, and the call is re-pinned to the running llama-server's origin (paths restricted to /v1/* and /health) over a loopback client with that server's per-session --api-key.

Agent mode runs a bounded tool loop (DEFAULT_MAX_ROUNDS 3, DEFAULT_MAX_TOOL_CALLS_PER_ROUND 12) over the tools search_paper, read_pages, scholarly_search (OpenAlex), lookup_doi (Crossref), fetch_url (untrusted content) and submit_annotations (carrying up to 5 schema_remarks); a separate judge model scores each new/changed, signature-deduped proposal as accept/revise/reject, and the loop exits on all-accept, the round budget, or an identical resubmission.

Agent submissions are deterministically verified: evidence must be an exact NFKC-normalized substring of what the agent was shown (or an ordered >=85% word match within a 40-word window), and a URL source must be among the pages actually fetched — a URL only seen in search results marks the suggestion webUnverified (unticked row) rather than failing it.

Classify mode sends only closed-answer questions to a System One decision model: booleans become noul questions and string enums with 2-255 options become choice questions; per-family profiles (modelProfiles.ts) bound state size, questions and options per request, ineligible or over-limit fields are reported 'not handled by <model>' rather than silently dropped, the state mode (full/abstract+body/abstract-only) is surfaced in the review, and confidence recorded is System One's own (noul or probs[choice]) — a Classify target can also serve as the cross-check model with a threshold (default 0.8) that unticks low-confidence rows.

The flags-only re-check (Prompt mode, opt-in, never persisted) double-checks already-answered fields: the model returns agree / disagree / unsure, and a disagree without a valid coerced proposed value differing from the current one plus a verbatim supporting quote is downgraded to unsure; a disagreement is only a proposal, applied only with approval and only when the field still equals the value the AI checked.

An in-flight batch persists across restarts (slr.llm.batch.<identity>.<seat>) so the dialog can resume it; above PERSIST_SIZE_CAP (2 MB serialized) the record drops its rows/notes/errors and resume re-runs the scope instead of replaying stale review rows. executeBatch (shared by run and resume) starts papers with a runPool concurrency (1-4, default 2), records skipped papers separately from failures, and stops starting new papers once spend exceeds the cap while the in-flight paper finishes.

Provider-native web search is a server tool enabled only for anthropic (web_search_20250305, WEB_SEARCH_MAX_USES 5) and openrouter (plugin {id:'web'} with url_citation annotations) when the slr.llm.websearch flag is on; src/llm/websearch.test.ts is the specification (no src/llm/websearch.ts exists), searches are billed by the provider on top of tokens, and the count is shown in the usage line and recorded as webSearches.

The optional schema-feedback option (slr.llm.feedback, default on) writes, once per review (on Apply and on unapplied close/Discard), a buildRunFeedback aggregate (per-field outcomes — applied, unticked, edited, left empty, rejected, judge verdicts, cross-check disagreements, up to 10 truncated edits, deduped schema remarks — sorted most troublesome first) via project:writeFeedback to annotations/feedback/run-<timestamp>-<id>.json: field paths, truncated values, counts and remarks only, no paper text or evidence quotes; a write failure never blocks Apply or Discard.

Retryable statuses (408/429/500/502/503/504/529) are retried at most 4 times with jittered backoff capped at 60 s, honoring the server's Retry-After (the retry_after_ms the Rust shell parses from a delta-seconds or HTTP-date header); a cross-check disagreement (unlike a fill failure) never fails the paper.

When a chat target's contextTokens is known, the paper is fitted to the window: chatInputBudget subtracts the system prompt (schema, rules, few-shot block), wrapper, reply reserve and THINK_RESERVE (4096, only with a reasoning effort); fitPaperText drops the reference list first, then trailing pages, then cuts inside page 1 keeping [page N] markers; below MIN_PAPER_TOKENS (256) the paper fails instead of being sent. Agent mode requires at least AGENT_MIN_CONTEXT (32,000 tokens) on annotator and judge, an Ollama target with unset Context to use blocks the run, and a reply whose prompt_eval_count is within 64 tokens of num_ctx sets inputTruncated and fails the paper so nothing from a truncated prompt reaches the review.
